Interface AsyncStreamingHttpClient

All Superinterfaces:
AsyncHttpClient, AutoCloseable, Closeable, LifeCycle<AsyncHttpClient>
public interface AsyncStreamingHttpClient extends AsyncHttpClient
The StreamingHttpClient with CompletionStage results and the body pulled one element at a time, instead of Reactive Streams: an AsyncHttpClient that also streams response bodies.

An exchange completes with the response, or its elements, once the status and the headers arrived. The body is a BodyElements cursor: the next element is read from the connection when BodyElements.next() is called, so nothing is decoded ahead of the caller. The connection stays reserved until the elements were read to the end or closed. The stages complete on a thread chosen by the client, usually an I/O thread: a consumer must not block.

When the response has an error status, the stage fails with an HttpClientResponseException carrying the response and its body, decoded into the error type.

It also reads server-sent events, the counterpart of SseClient, and the elements of JSON streams with their response.

An instance is obtained from a StreamingHttpClient with StreamingHttpClient.toAsyncStreaming(), or injected.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • exchangeStream

      <I> CompletionStage<HttpResponse<BodyElements<ByteBuffer<?>>>> exchangeStream(HttpRequest<I> request, Argument<?> errorType)
      Perform an HTTP request and read the response body as its bytes arrive, see StreamingHttpClient.exchangeStream(HttpRequest, Argument). The elements are the pieces of the body as they were received, as heap buffers that are not reference counted.
      Type Parameters:
      I - The request body type
      Parameters:
      request - The HttpRequest to execute
      errorType - The type that the response body should be coerced into if the server responds with an error
      Returns:
      A CompletionStage that completes with the response, whose body is the pieces of the response body

    • exchangeEventStream

      default <I,B> CompletionStage<HttpResponse<BodyElements<Event<B>>>> exchangeEventStream(HttpRequest<I> request, Argument<B> eventType, Argument<?> errorType)
      Perform an HTTP request whose response is either a stream of server-sent events or a single body, see SseClient.exchangeEventStream(HttpRequest, Argument, Argument).
      • The Accept header of the request is kept when it accepts text/event-stream, for example application/json, text/event-stream. Otherwise text/event-stream is added to it.
      • When the content type of the response is text/event-stream, the elements are the events of the body, each decoded as it is read. The data of an event is decoded as JSON into the event type.
      • Otherwise the whole body is decoded into the event type, using the content type of the response, and is the only element.
      • When the body holds no event, for example a 202 Accepted response, the elements are empty.

      The default implementation reads the pieces of exchangeStream(HttpRequest, Argument) and decodes them as server-sent events, the data with the default JsonMapper. This fallback has no bean context; implementations with an injected message body handler registry override it to use their configured readers.

      Type Parameters:
      I - The request body type
      B - The event data type
      Parameters:
      request - The HttpRequest to execute
      eventType - The event data type
      errorType - The type that the response body should be coerced into if the server responds with an error
      Returns:
      A CompletionStage that completes with the response, whose body is the events
